slides.say: Rectangle A B C D consists of six congruent rectangles, arranged as in the accompanying figure. The perimeter of A B C D is forty centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?

The main difficulty here is to see that each small rectangle has a fixed ratio between its long side and its short side. That ratio comes from the way the six rectangles fit together. [short pause] We'll find the ratio first, and then the perimeter and the area.
[short pause] Call the short side of a small rectangle x. Look at one of the lying rectangles in the middle. Its short side is x. All six are the same, so each of the four lying rectangles is x high.
at: Look at one of the lying rectangles
each of the four lying rectangles

slides.say: Now look at a standing rectangle on the side. Its long side is as tall as the four lying rectangles together, four x's. So the long side is four x, and the ratio is one to four.
at: Now look at a standing rectangle

slides.say: Now every side of A B C D. The height is four x. Across, there's x, then four x, then x again, so the width is six x.
at: Now every side of A B C D

slides.say: The perimeter is two times, four x plus six x, which is twenty x. It's forty, so x is two.

Careful, nobody asked for x, and two isn't even a choice. They asked for the area. Base times height: four x is eight, and six x is twelve. Eight times twelve is ninety-six. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Once we have the sides as four x and six x, there's a shorter way to finish. The sides are in the ratio two to three. Half the perimeter, one height plus one width, is twenty.
at: The sides are in the ratio two

slides.say: Two parts plus three parts is five parts, and five parts are twenty, so one part is four. The sides are two times four, eight, and three times four, twelve. Eight times twelve is ninety-six again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
